ranking.note: Raised to P1: pinning/censorship resistance in package relay is the category's first criterion, and it blocks CPFP fee-bumps that L2 depends on until the next block.
Lowered to P3: policy expansion with no cited downstream demand (revisits closed #27926), weaker than the P2 bug fixes and the incentive-compatibility rationale of #36540.
Lowered to P4: speculative draft for an unratified soft fork, author states it is not for merge and it vendors unmerged libsecp work; mempool policy is incidental to it.

inconsistencies: #36367 and #36538 both fix signed-integer overflows that trip Assume aborts in mempool/cluster fee arithmetic; they should be reviewed together, #36367 first since it touches the cluster FeeFrac accumulation path that #36538's staging reorder also depends on.

#36328 (package transactions trimmed by size limits) and #36214 (cluster trimming during reorgs) exercise the same trimming logic from opposite sides; reviewing #36328 first clarifies the expected behaviour the tests in #36214 should pin down.

#35581 is driven by block-template/mining needs and only touches mempool via a new update signal; its value is mostly outside this category, which is why it sits low among the P3s despite being a performance change.

#36122 and #36466 both loosen Taproot witness standardness, but they are independent: #36466 is a standalone relay-policy decision while #36122 depends on consensus acceptance of BIP460; they should not be bundled.
result.notes: Only one PR reaches P1; the remaining bug fixes are real but config- or reorg-conditioned, so they cluster in P2 rather than being flattened upward. The P3 block is genuinely deferrable tooling, tests and policy relaxations with weak external demand.
